Name: layer_ablation_function
Title: Which Layer of Evo2 Encodes Gene Function? A Layer-wise Ablation Study
Experiment: Extract embeddings from four different Evo2-7B layers: an early layer (blocks.4.mlp.l3), two middle layers (blocks.14.mlp.l3, blocks.21.mlp.l3), and the late layer used in the baseline (blocks.28.mlp.l3). Train the same MLP classifier on each set of embeddings with identical hyperparameters and train/test splits. Compare AUROC, accuracy, and F1 across layers. Additionally, compute a one-hot nucleotide baseline (4-mer frequency features from the promoter+CDS sequence) to establish a non-learned lower bound. Plot AUROC vs. layer depth to reveal whether functional information accumulates progressively through the network or emerges at a specific depth.

Name: embedding_geometry_functional_coherence
Title: Does Evo2 Embedding Geometry Reflect Functional Gene Relationships? A Multi-Class Clustering Analysis
Experiment: Extend the dataset to 4 functional gene classes: DNA repair (existing), tumor suppressors (existing), cell cycle (KEGG hsa04110), and apoptosis (KEGG hsa04210). Balance classes by sampling up to 50 genes per class if available. Extract embeddings using blocks.28.mlp.l3. Modify build_dataset() to fetch the two new classes. Compute three key metrics using cosine similarity: (1) Silhouette score across all classes to quantify cluster coherence (range -1 to 1, >0.5 is good); (2) ratio of mean within-class cosine distance to mean between-class distance (should be <0.5 if classes separate well); (3) k-nearest neighbor purity for k=5 and k=10 (fraction of neighbors with same label, >0.6 indicates functional coherence). Compare each metric against a random baseline with shuffled labels (1000 permutations, compute p-values). Generate a 2D UMAP projection colored by functional class. Output: JSON with metrics, p-values, and per-class statistics; UMAP visualization saved as PNG. This tests whether Evo2 embeddings organize genes by function in a geometrically meaningful way.

Name: sequence_region_ablation
Title: Promoter vs. Coding Sequence: Which Genomic Region Drives Functional Gene Classification in Evo2 Embeddings?
Experiment: Modify get_gene_sequence() to return three sequence variants per gene: (1) promoter-only (2kb upstream of TSS), (2) CDS-only, and (3) promoter+CDS concatenated (baseline). Update build_dataset() to cache all three variants. In run(), add a 'sequence_type' argument to select which variant to embed. Train the MLP classifier on embeddings from each sequence type separately using identical hyperparameters, train/test splits, and random seeds. Run across 3 seeds for each of the 3 sequence types (9 total runs). Compute AUROC, accuracy, and F1 for each condition. Report mean±stderr across seeds. To address sequence length confounding, also report mean sequence lengths for each region type and add an optional control experiment where CDS is truncated to 2kb from the start codon. Output: JSON with performance metrics for each sequence type, plus a bar plot comparing AUROC across the three conditions. Use paired t-test to determine if promoter+CDS significantly outperforms individual regions. This reveals whether Evo2 encodes functional information primarily from regulatory sequences (promoter), protein-coding constraints (CDS), or synergistically from both.

Name: kmer_vs_embedding_comparison
Title: Do Evo2 Embeddings Capture Information Beyond K-mer Composition? A Comparative and Hybrid Modeling Analysis
Experiment: Implement a k-mer baseline and hybrid model to test whether embeddings encode information beyond simple sequence composition. (1) Add extract_kmer_features(sequences, k=6) that computes hexamer frequency vectors (count/total_kmers) from full sequences, then filters to the top 500 most frequent hexamers across the dataset to avoid high-dimensional overfitting. (2) Modify run() to support three model types via a 'feature_type' argument: 'embedding' (baseline MLP on Evo2 embeddings), 'kmer' (logistic regression on k-mer features with L2 regularization, C=1.0), and 'hybrid' (MLP on concatenated k-mer features + embeddings). (3) For the k-mer model, extract the top 30 most discriminative hexamers by absolute logistic regression coefficient values from the trained model. (4) On the training set only, compute mutual information between each of the top 30 k-mers (binarized at median frequency: above median = 1) and class labels using sklearn.feature_selection.mutual_info_classif. (5) Compute mean Pearson correlation between k-mer feature vectors and embedding vectors across all samples to quantify linear k-mer encoding. (6) Run all three model types with identical train/test splits across 3 random seeds. Output: JSON with mean±stderr performance (AUROC, accuracy, F1) for each model type, top 30 discriminative k-mers with coefficients and MI scores, mean k-mer-embedding correlation, and a bar plot comparing the three approaches. Use paired t-test for significance. This reveals whether Evo2 embeddings are primarily compositional or capture higher-order sequence patterns.

Name: functional_transfer_generalization
Title: Do Evo2 Embeddings Enable Cross-Function Transfer Learning? Testing Classifier Generalization to Unseen Gene Classes
Experiment: Test whether a classifier trained on one pair of functional classes can distinguish a different pair, revealing if embeddings encode transferable functional relationships. (1) Modify build_dataset() to fetch four functional classes: DNA repair (train, label=0), TSG (train, label=1), cell cycle genes (KEGG hsa04110, held-out, label=0), and apoptosis genes (KEGG hsa04210, held-out, label=1). Mark held-out genes with a 'split' field. (2) Train the MLP classifier only on DNA repair vs TSG with the baseline configuration. (3) Apply the trained classifier (without retraining) to embeddings of held-out cell cycle and apoptosis genes. Compute predicted probabilities for each held-out gene. (4) Calculate transfer AUROC treating cell cycle as negative class (0) and apoptosis as positive class (1), using the predicted probabilities from the DNA repair vs TSG classifier. (5) Statistical test: compare transfer AUROC against chance (0.5) using a permutation test (shuffle held-out labels 1000 times, compute null distribution, report p-value). (6) Compute the same transfer AUROC for two baselines: (a) k-mer logistic regression trained on DNA repair vs TSG, applied to held-out classes; (b) random classifier (uniform random probabilities). (7) Generate a 2D UMAP with all four classes colored separately to visualize embedding space organization. Output: JSON with transfer AUROC for Evo2, k-mer, and random baselines, p-value, confusion matrix on held-out set, and UMAP visualization. Transfer AUROC significantly above 0.5 indicates embeddings capture generalizable functional structure.

Name: sequence_perturbation_sensitivity
Title: What Sequence Features Drive Evo2 Functional Classification? A Perturbation-Based Sensitivity Analysis
Experiment: Test which sequence features Evo2 embeddings are sensitive to via controlled perturbations. (1) Select 10 high-confidence correctly classified genes per class (classifier probability >0.9 across all 3 seeds from baseline run). (2) For each gene, generate 5 sequence perturbations: (a) GC-matched shuffling of promoter (preserve dinucleotide frequencies using uShuffle algorithm or simple Markov chain shuffling), (b) replace promoter with a random promoter from the opposite class, (c) GC-matched shuffling of CDS (preserve codon usage by shuffling synonymous codons within each codon family), (d) reverse-complement the entire sequence, (e) truncate to remove the first 500bp of promoter. (3) Extract embeddings for all perturbed sequences using the same Evo2 layer (blocks.28.mlp.l3). (4) Apply the trained baseline classifier to perturbed embeddings and record predicted probabilities. (5) Compute 'prediction shift' for each perturbation type: mean absolute change in predicted probability compared to original sequence. (6) Statistical test: use Friedman test (non-parametric repeated measures ANOVA) across genes to determine if perturbation types cause significantly different prediction shifts, followed by post-hoc Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Bonferroni correction. (7) Compute embedding space displacement: mean cosine distance between original and perturbed embeddings for each perturbation type. Output: JSON with mean±stderr prediction shifts and embedding displacements for each perturbation type, statistical test results (p-values, effect sizes), and a grouped bar plot showing prediction shift by perturbation type and class. A box plot showing per-gene prediction shifts across perturbation types. If promoter swapping causes large shifts but CDS shuffling does not, this indicates Evo2 relies primarily on promoter-encoded information. Reverse-complement serves as a control for strand-specific vs. composition-only encoding.
